en.t: Inversion for emphasis: Never have I
en.g: Add drama and emphasis with inversion: Never have I, Not only... but also.
p: Negative or limiting word first, then auxiliary + subject: Never have I tasted anything so good. Rarely do I watch TV.
Not only + auxiliary + subject, but also: Not only did we win, but we also broke the record.
It's formal or dramatic, great for stories and speeches: Little did she know... No sooner had I left than it rained.
en.q: Complete this dramatically: Never have I ever... What's the most amazing thing you've seen?
en.c: Rewrite three normal sentences with inversion, e.g. I have never been so happy → Never have I been so happy.

en.t: Cleft sentences: What I need is
en.g: Highlight the key part of a sentence with cleft sentences.
p: What-clefts: What I love is travelling. What surprised me was the silence. What we need is more time.
It-clefts point to the focus: It was Maria who organised the party (not someone else). It's the weather that I miss.
Spoken favourites: The thing is,... All I want is... The reason why I came is... The best part was...
en.q: What do you love most about where you live? Start your answer with What I love about... is...
en.c: Write four cleft sentences about your life: two What... is/was and two It was... who/that.

Beliebt im Gespräch: The thing is,... All I want is... The reason why I came is... The best part was...
de.q: Was liebst du am meisten an deinem Wohnort? Beginne deine Antwort mit What I love about... is...

es.c: Escribe cuatro oraciones escindidas sobre tu vida: dos con What... is/was y dos con It was... who/that.

en.g: Shorten sentences elegantly with participle clauses like Having finished work.
p: -ing for actions at the same time or a reason: Walking along the beach, we found a shell. Feeling hungry, I made a sandwich.
Having + past participle for an earlier action: Having finished my homework, I watched a film.
Past participle for a passive meaning: Painted in 1503, the Mona Lisa is world-famous. Both parts need the same subject!
en.q: Describe your morning with a participle clause, e.g. Having had breakfast, I... What did you do next?
en.c: Join three pairs of sentences with participle clauses, e.g. I finished work. I went home. → Having finished work, I went home.

de.g: Mit Partizipialsätzen wie Having finished work kürzt du Sätze elegant.
p: -ing für Gleichzeitiges oder einen Grund: Walking along the beach, we found a shell. Feeling hungry, I made a sandwich.
Having + Partizip für eine frühere Handlung: Having finished my homework, I watched a film.
Partizip Perfekt mit Passivbedeutung: Painted in 1503, the Mona Lisa is world-famous. Beide Teile brauchen dasselbe Subjekt!
de.q: Beschreib deinen Morgen mit einem Partizipialsatz, z. B. Having had breakfast, I... Was hast du danach gemacht?
de.c: Verbinde drei Satzpaare mit Partizipialsätzen, z. B. I finished work. I went home. → Having finished work, I went home.

es.q: Describe tu mañana con una oración de participio, p. ej. Having had breakfast, I... ¿Qué hiciste después?
es.c: Une tres pares de frases con participio, p. ej. I finished work. I went home. → Having finished work, I went home.

en.g: Use refined relative clauses like most of whom, some of which and the reason why.
p: Quantifier + of whom (people) / of which (things): I have many friends, a few of whom speak Japanese.
Formal preposition first: the city in which I was born = the city I was born in. The person to whom I spoke.
Which for a whole idea: It rained all week, which was disappointing. Use commas with these extra-information clauses.
en.q: Tell me about a group of people you know, using most of whom or some of whom.
en.c: Write four sentences with most of whom, some of which, the reason why and a which that refers to a whole idea.

Formell steht die Präposition vorn: the city in which I was born = the city I was born in. The person to whom I spoke.
Which für einen ganzen Gedanken: It rained all week, which was disappointing. Solche Zusatzsätze stehen mit Kommas.

en.g: Master tricky article cases with places, institutions and abstract ideas.
p: Institutions used for their purpose take no article: go to school, be in bed, go to church, at work. The school = the building.
Places: no article for most countries, cities, lakes and single mountains (France, Lake Garda, Everest).
The with rivers, seas, oceans, ranges and plural countries: the Nile, the Alps, the USA. Abstract ideas in general: Love is..., Music helps.
en.q: Where did you go to school, and do you ever go back to the school to visit?
en.c: Write five sentences with tricky articles: school vs the school, a lake, a river, a mountain range and an abstract idea.

de.g: Du meisterst knifflige Artikelfälle bei Orten, Institutionen und abstrakten Begriffen.
p: Institutionen in ihrem Zweck ohne Artikel: go to school, be in bed, go to church, at work. The school = das Gebäude.
Orte: kein Artikel bei den meisten Ländern, Städten, Seen und einzelnen Bergen (France, Lake Garda, Everest).
The bei Flüssen, Meeren, Gebirgen und Ländern im Plural: the Nile, the Alps, the USA. Abstraktes allgemein: Love is..., Music helps.
de.q: Wo bist du zur Schule gegangen, und besuchst du die Schule manchmal noch?

The con ríos, mares, cordilleras y países en plural: the Nile, the Alps, the USA. Ideas abstractas en general: Love is..., Music helps.

es.c: Escribe cinco frases con artículos difíciles: school frente a the school, un lago, un río, una cordillera y una idea abstracta.

en.g: Use advanced modals: needn't have vs didn't need to, would rather and had better.
p: Needn't have + past participle: you did it, but it wasn't necessary. I needn't have cooked: they'd already eaten.
Didn't need to: it wasn't necessary, so you probably didn't do it. I didn't need to queue, so I went straight in.
Would rather + verb (preference): I'd rather walk. Had better = strong advice: You'd better hurry.
en.q: Would you rather spend a weekend in the mountains or by the sea? Why?
en.c: Write four sentences: one with needn't have, one with didn't need to, one with I'd rather and one with you'd better.

de.g: Du nutzt fortgeschrittene Modalverben: needn't have vs. didn't need to, would rather und had better.
p: Needn't have + Partizip: Du hast es getan, es war aber unnötig. I needn't have cooked: they'd already eaten.
Didn't need to: Es war nicht nötig, also hast du es wohl nicht getan. I didn't need to queue, so I went straight in.
Would rather + Verb (Vorliebe): I'd rather walk. Had better = dringender Rat: You'd better hurry.

Didn't need to: no hacía falta, así que seguramente no lo hiciste. I didn't need to queue, so I went straight in.
Would rather + verbo (preferencia): I'd rather walk. Had better = consejo fuerte: You'd better hurry.
es.q: ¿Preferirías pasar un fin de semana en la montaña o en la playa? ¿Por qué?

en.g: Tell nostalgic stories about past habits with would.
p: Would + verb for repeated past actions: When I was little, we would spend summers at my grandparents' house.
Would is only for actions, not states: I used to love sweets (not I would love). We used to have a dog.
Start with used to, then continue with would: We used to go camping. We'd wake up early and we'd swim in the river.
en.q: What would you do on summer holidays when you were a child?
en.c: Write a nostalgic paragraph of five sentences about your childhood: start with used to, then use would three times.

en.t: Be used to vs get used to
en.g: Tell apart be used to, get used to and used to.
p: Be used to + -ing or noun = it's normal for me: I'm used to the cold. I'm used to working at night.
Get used to = the process of it becoming normal: I'm getting used to my new job. I soon got used to the food.
Don't confuse with used to + verb (past habit): I used to drive (I don't now) vs I'm used to driving (it's easy for me).
en.q: What's something new in your life that you're still getting used to?
en.c: Write three sentences about yourself: one with I'm used to, one with I'm getting used to and one with I used to.

de.t: Be used to vs get used to
de.g: Du unterscheidest be used to, get used to und used to.
p: Be used to + -ing oder Nomen = für mich normal: I'm used to the cold. I'm used to working at night.
Get used to = der Prozess, sich zu gewöhnen: I'm getting used to my new job. I soon got used to the food.
Nicht verwechseln mit used to + Verb (früher): I used to drive (heute nicht mehr) vs. I'm used to driving (fällt mir leicht).
de.q: An welche neue Sache in deinem Leben gewöhnst du dich gerade noch?
de.c: Schreib drei Sätze über dich: mit I'm used to, mit I'm getting used to und mit I used to.

Get used to = el proceso de acostumbrarse: I'm getting used to my new job. I soon got used to the food.
No lo confundas con used to + verbo (hábito pasado): I used to drive (ya no) frente a I'm used to driving (me resulta fácil).
es.q: ¿A qué cosa nueva de tu vida te estás acostumbrando todavía?
es.c: Escribe tres frases sobre ti: con I'm used to, con I'm getting used to y con I used to.

en.t: Discourse markers: on the other hand
en.g: Structure what you say with discourse markers like on the other hand and nevertheless.
p: Adding and contrasting: Moreover, furthermore, what's more... On the other hand, nevertheless, having said that...
Correcting or surprising: As a matter of fact, actually, in fact. As a matter of fact, I've never tried sushi.
Summing up: On the whole, all in all, overall. They work in speech and writing and make you sound fluent and organised.
en.q: Is it better to live in a big city or a small town? Answer using moreover, on the other hand and on the whole.
en.c: Give a 30-second spoken opinion on any topic using four markers: moreover, nevertheless, as a matter of fact and on the whole.

de.t: Discourse markers: on the other hand
de.g: Mit Diskursmarkern wie on the other hand und nevertheless strukturierst du, was du sagst.
p: Hinzufügen und kontrastieren: Moreover, furthermore, what's more... On the other hand, nevertheless, having said that...
Korrigieren oder überraschen: As a matter of fact, actually, in fact. As a matter of fact, I've never tried sushi.
Zusammenfassen: On the whole, all in all, overall. Sie wirken in Rede und Text und lassen dich flüssig und klar klingen.
de.q: Lebt man besser in einer Großstadt oder in einer Kleinstadt? Antworte mit moreover, on the other hand und on the whole.
de.c: Sprich 30 Sekunden lang deine Meinung zu einem Thema mit vier Markern: moreover, nevertheless, as a matter of fact und on the whole.

es.q: ¿Es mejor vivir en una gran ciudad o en un pueblo? Responde con moreover, on the other hand y on the whole.
es.c: Da tu opinión en voz alta durante 30 segundos con cuatro marcadores: moreover, nevertheless, as a matter of fact y on the whole.
